title: Feige's sharp unit-slack inequality
abstract: For small-universe probability spaces, proves the sharp fixed-dimensional unit-slack lower bound for sums of independent nonnegative random variables: if each coordinate has mean at most one, then the probability that the sum lies below its mean plus one is at least (n/(n+1))^n, and this constant is optimal. The supporting library formalizes the Vlassis--Thomas exact distribution-free calibration theorem, Grünbaum's centroid-halfspace inequality and sharp simplex example, and the normalized-exponential bridge joining them.

informal.Feige.sharp_unit_slack_feige_complete: For every positive dimension n and every small-universe probability space, the sharp fixed-dimensional lower bound for the strict event that a sum of independent nonnegative random variables is below its expectation plus one is (n/(n+1))^n, and an explicit finite family proves optimality.
informal.VlassisThomas.exactCalibration: On every small-universe probability space, the Dirichlet statistic used in the proof is super-uniform for every independent family of measurable, integrable, nonnegative random variables whose coordinate means are at most one.
informal.Grunbaum.grunbaum_centroid_halfspace: Every closed halfspace containing the centroid of a positive-volume convex body in finite-dimensional Euclidean space contains at least the sharp Grünbaum fraction of the body's volume.
